body.text: Prātimokṣasūtram*
body.translated_text: <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s>*

body.text: namo bhagavate vītarāgāya /
body.translated_text: Homage to the Blessed One, the one free from passion.

children.text: narendradevendrasuvanditena trilokavighuṣṭaviśālakīrtinā /
children.translated_text: By him who is venerated by the lords of men and the lords of gods, whose vast fame resounds through the three worlds,

children.text: buddhena lokārthacareṇa tāyinā sudeśitaṃ prātimokṣaṃ vidunā // 1 //
children.translated_text: by the <s>Buddha</s>, the protector who acts for the benefit of the world, the wise one — the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> has been well taught. // 1 //

children.text: taṃ prātimokṣaṃ bhavaduḥkhamokṣaṃ śrutvāna dhīrāḥ sugatasya bhāṣitaṃ /
children.translated_text: Having heard that <s>Prātimokṣa</s>, which is liberation from the suffering of existence, the teaching spoken by the <s>Sugata</s>,

children.text: ṣaḍindriyasaṃvarasaṃvṛtatvāt karonti jātīmaraṇasya antaṃ // 2 //
children.translated_text: through being restrained by the restraint of the six sense-faculties, the steadfast ones make an end of birth and death. // 2 //

children.text: cirasya labdhvā ratanāni trīṇi buddhotpādaṃ mānuṣikāñ ca śraddhāṃ /
children.translated_text: Having obtained, after a long time, the three jewels — the arising of a <s>Buddha</s>, human birth, and faith —

children.text: dauḥśīlyavadyaṃ parivarjayitvā viśuddhaśīlā bhavathāpramattāḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned the fault of bad conduct, be of purified conduct and heedful! // 3 //

children.text: śīlena yukto śramaṇo 'tiveti śīlena yukto brāhmaṇo 'tiveti /
children.translated_text: An ascetic endowed with moral conduct surpasses [all]; a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> endowed with moral conduct surpasses [all];

children.text: śīlena yukto naradevapūjyo śīlena yuktasya hi prātimokṣaṃ // 4 //
children.translated_text: one endowed with moral conduct is worthy of worship by gods and men; for one endowed with moral conduct there is the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>. // 4 //

children.text: anekabuddhānumataṃ viśuddhaṃ śīlaṃ pratiṣṭhā dharaṇīva sānuṃ /
children.translated_text: The moral conduct approved by countless <s>Buddhas</s>, pure, a foundation like the earth with its mountains —

children.text: udāhariṣyāmy ahaṃ saṃghamadhye hitāya lokasya sadevakasya // 5 //
children.translated_text: I shall recite it in the midst of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, for the benefit of the world together with its gods. // 5 //

body.text: [iti] upodghātaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the introduction.

children.text: kiṃ jīvitena teṣāṃ yeṣām ihākuśalamūlajālāni /
children.translated_text: What is the use of life for those whose nets of unwholesome roots

children.text: pracchādayanti hṛdayaṃ gaganam iva samunnatā meghāḥ //
children.translated_text: cover the heart, like towering clouds [covering] the sky?

children.text: atijīvitaṃ ca teṣāṃ yeṣām ihākuśalamūlajālāni /
children.translated_text: But life is well-lived for those whose nets of unwholesome roots

children.text: vilayaṃ vrajanti kṣipraṃ divasakarahatāndhakāram iva // 6-7 //
children.translated_text: quickly dissolve, like darkness destroyed by the sun. // 6-7 //

children.text: kiṃ poṣadhena teṣāṃ ye te sāvadyaśīlacaritrāḥ /
children.translated_text: What is the use of the <s>Poṣadha</s> for those whose conduct and moral character are blameworthy,

children.text: jarāmaraṇapañjaragatā amaravitarkehi khādyanti //
children.translated_text: who, caught in the cage of old age and death, are devoured by thoughts of immortality?

children.text: kāryaṃ ca poṣadhena teṣāṃ ye te anavadyaśīlacāritrāḥ /
children.translated_text: But the <s>Poṣadha</s> is necessary for those whose conduct and moral character are blameless,

children.text: jarāmaraṇāntakarā mārabalapramardanā dhīrāḥ // 8-9 //
children.translated_text: who make an end of old age and death, who crush the power of <s>Māra</s> — the steadfast ones. // 8-9 //

children.text: kiṃ poṣadhena teṣām alajjināṃ bhinnavṛttaśīlānāṃ /
children.translated_text: What is the use of the <s>Poṣadha</s> for those who are shameless, whose observances and moral conduct are broken,

children.text: mithyājīvaratānām asaraṇam iva carantānāṃ //
children.translated_text: who delight in wrong livelihood, who wander as if without refuge?

children.text: kāryaṃ ca poṣadhena teṣāṃ lajjinām abhinnavṛttaśīlānāṃ /
children.translated_text: But the <s>Poṣadha</s> is necessary for those who have a sense of shame, whose observances and moral conduct are unbroken,

children.text: samyagjīvaratānām adhyāśayaśuddhaśīlānāṃ // 10-11 //
children.translated_text: who delight in right livelihood, whose moral conduct is pure in intention. // 10-11 //

children.text: kiṃ poṣadhena teṣāṃ ye te duḥśīlapāpakarmāntāḥ /
children.translated_text: What is the use of the <s>Poṣadha</s> for those who are of bad conduct and evil deeds,

children.text: kuṇapam iva samudrato samutkṣiptāḥ śāstu prāvacanāt //
children.translated_text: who are cast out from the Teacher's dispensation like a corpse from the ocean?

children.text: kāryaṃ ca poṣadhena teṣāṃ ye te traidhātuke anupaliptāḥ /
children.translated_text: But the <s>Poṣadha</s> is necessary for those who are unattached in the three realms of existence,

children.text: ākāśe viya pāṇi śuddhānāṃ vimuktacittānāṃ // 12-13 //
children.translated_text: like the hand in space — for the pure ones, those whose minds are liberated. // 12-13 //

children.text: kiṃ poṣadhena teṣāṃ ṣaḍindriyaṃ yehi yehi surakṣitaṃ nityaṃ /
children.translated_text: What is the use of the <s>Poṣadha</s> for those by whom the six sense-faculties are always well-guarded,

children.text: patitānāṃ māraviṣaye svagocaraṃ varjayantānāṃ //
children.translated_text: [yet who are] fallen into <s>Māra</s>'s domain, abandoning their own proper sphere?

children.text: kāryaṃ ca poṣadhena teṣāṃ ṣaḍindriyaṃ yehi surakṣitaṃ nityaṃ /
children.translated_text: But the <s>Poṣadha</s> is necessary for those by whom the six sense-faculties are always well-guarded,

children.text: yuktānāṃ śāstur vacane jinavacane śāsanaratānāṃ // 14-15 //
children.translated_text: who are diligent in the Teacher's word, who delight in the instruction of the <s>Jina</s>'s teaching. // 14-15 //

children.text: kiṃ poṣadhena teṣām ātmaśīlehi ye hy upavadanti /
children.translated_text: What is the use of the <s>Poṣadha</s> for those who reproach [others] regarding their own moral conduct,

children.text: sabrahmacāriṇaś ca śastā devamanuṣyāś ca duḥśīlāḥ //
children.translated_text: and [who reproach] their fellow practitioners of the holy life — the Teacher, gods, and men — [those who are] of bad conduct?

children.text: kāryaṃ ca poṣadhena teṣāṃ śīlehi nāsti gārhyaṃ /
children.translated_text: But the <s>Poṣadha</s> is necessary for those in whose moral conduct there is nothing blameworthy,

children.text: sarvatra nopavadyā vijñānāṃ vai sadevake loke // 16-17 //
children.translated_text: who are nowhere to be reproached by the wise in the world together with its gods. // 16-17 //

children.text: kiṃ poṣadhena teṣāṃ virāgitaṃ śāstuḥ śāsanaṃ yehi /
children.translated_text: What is the use of the <s>Poṣadha</s> for those by whom the Teacher's dispensation is disregarded,

children.text: āsevitā ca yehi vipattīyo pañca cāpattīḥ //
children.translated_text: and by whom the five misfortunes and offenses have been cultivated?

children.text: kāryaṃ ca poṣadhena teṣāṃ yuktānāṃ śāsane daśabalasya /
children.translated_text: But the <s>Poṣadha</s> is necessary for those who are diligent in the dispensation of the one with ten powers,

children.text: sarvajñasya sarvadarśino maitrīpadā yehi paricīrṇāḥ // 18-19 //
children.translated_text: the Omniscient One, the All-Seeing One — those by whom the stages of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) have been practiced. // 18-19 //

children.text: yeṣāṃ ca vasati hṛdaye śāstā dharmo gaṇottamo /
children.translated_text: For those in whose hearts dwell the Teacher, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the supreme <s>Saṅgha</s>,

children.text: śikṣā uddeśo saṃvāso saṃbhogo śāstuno vacanaṃ //
children.translated_text: the training, the recitation, the communal life, the shared use [of requisites], and the word of the Teacher —

children.text: teṣām upoṣadho 'dya aparityaktāni yehi etāni /
children.translated_text: for them is the <s>Upoṣadha</s> today — those by whom these things have not been abandoned;

children.text: paricarya dharmarājaṃ te yānti asaṃskṛtaṃ sthānaṃ // 20-21 //
children.translated_text: serving the King of <s>Dharma</s>, they go to the unconditioned state. // 20-21 //

children.text: śuddhasya vai sadā phalguḥ sadā śuddhasya poṣadho /
children.translated_text: For the pure one, the <s>Poṣadha</s> is always trifling; for the always-pure one, the <s>Poṣadha</s> [is easy];

children.text: śuddhasya śucikarmasya sadā sampadyate vrataṃ // 22 //
children.translated_text: for the pure one whose deeds are clean, the observance is always fulfilled. // 22 //

children.text: yāvat sūtrapratikṣepo gaṇamadhye na bheṣyati /
children.translated_text: As long as rejection of the <s>Sūtra</s> does not arise in the midst of the <s>Saṅgha</s>,

children.text: tāvat sthāsyati saddharmo sāmagrī ca gaṇottame // 23 //
children.translated_text: so long will the true <s>Dharma</s> endure, and harmony in the supreme <s>Saṅgha</s>. // 23 //

children.text: yāvac ca deśayitāraḥ pratipattāraś ca dharmaratnasya /
children.translated_text: And as long as there are teachers and practitioners of the jewel of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: tāvat sthāsyati saddharmmo hitāya sarvalokasya // 24 //
children.translated_text: so long will the true <s>Dharma</s> endure for the benefit of the entire world. // 24 //

children.text: tasmāt samagrāḥ sahitāḥ sagauravāḥ bhaviyā anyamanyaṃ paricaratha /
children.translated_text: Therefore, united, harmonious, and respectful, serve one another;

children.text: dharmarājam adhigacchatha nirvāṇam atandritā acyutam padam aśokam iti // 25 //
children.translated_text: attain the King of <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — the unwearied, immovable, sorrowless state. // 25 //

body.text: (iti) vastu /
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the subject matter.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)Einl. abhikrāntāḥ suvihitāḥ śuddhā nipuṇā anusaṅgāyanto upaniṣaṇṇā, cāritāḥ śalākā, gaṇitā bhikḥū sīmāprāptā ettakā janāḥ / anāgatānām āyuḥmanto bhikḥūṇāṃ cchandapāriśuddhim ārocettha, ārocitaṃ ca prativedetha / ko bhikḥu bhikḥuṇīnāṃ cchandahārako? nāsti cātra kaścid anupasaṃpanno nāsti utkḥiptako / nāsti mātṛghātī, nāsti pitṛghātī / nāsti arhantaghātako, nāsti saṃghabhedako, nāsti tathāgatasya duḥṭacittarudhirotpādako / nāsti bhikḥuṇīdūḥako / nāsti stainyasaṃvāsiko, nāsti nānāsaṃvāsiko, nāsti asaṃvāsiko / nāsti tīrthikāpakrāntako / nāsti svayaṃsannaddhako / tad evaṃ samanvāharantu bhagavato śrāvakāṇāṃ nityaviśuddhānāṃ pariśuddhaśīlānāṃ /
body.translated_text: [The monks] have come forward, are well-disposed, pure, attentive, reciting together, and seated; the voting-sticks have been distributed, the <s>bhikṣus</s> counted, those within the boundary [are] so many persons. Venerable ones, announce the consent and purity of the <s>bhikṣus</s> who have not come, and report what has been announced. Which <s>bhikṣu</s> carries the consent of the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>? And there is here no one who is not fully ordained; there is no one who is suspended; there is no matricide; there is no patricide; there is no killer of an <s>Arhat</s>; there is no schismatic of the <s>Saṅgha</s>; there is no one who has with evil intent shed the blood of a <s>Tathāgata</s>; there is no corrupter of a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>; there is no one living in stealth; there is no one of different communion; there is no one who is without communion; there is no one who has gone over to the heretics; there is no one who has armed himself. Let [the assembly] thus consider that the disciples of the Blessed One are ever-pure and of purified conduct.

body.text: śṛṇotu me bhante saṃgho Ō adya saṃghasya cāturdaśiko vā sandhipoṣadho vā viśuddhinakṣatraṃ / ettakaṃ ṛtusya nirgataṃ / etta[ka]m avaśiṣṭaṃ / kiṃ saṃghasya pūrvakṛtyaṃ? alpakṛtyo bhagavataḥ śrāvakasaṃgho so bhavati /
body.translated_text: Let the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> hear me. Today is the <s>Saṅgha</s>'s fourteenth-day or junction <s>Poṣadha</s>, [on] the purification-constellation. So much of the season has passed; so much remains. What is the preliminary duty of the <s>Saṅgha</s>? The <s>Saṅgha</s> of disciples of the Blessed One is one of few duties.

body.text: śṛṇotu me bhante saṃgho Ō adya saṃghasya pāñcadaśiko poṣadho viśuddhinakṣatraṃ / yadi saṃghasya prāptakālaṃ saṃgho imasmin pṛthivīpradeśe yāvatakaṃ bhikṣusaṃghenābhigṛhītaṃ samantanavyāmamātraṃ atrāntare pāñcadaśikaṃ poṣadhaṃ kuryāt prātimokṣaṃ ca sūtram uddiśeyyā / ovayikā eṣā jñaptiḥ /
body.translated_text: Let the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> hear me. Today is the <s>Saṅgha</s>'s fifteenth-day <s>Poṣadha</s>, [on] the purification-constellation. If the time is proper for the <s>Saṅgha</s>, the <s>Saṅgha</s> should perform the fifteenth-day <s>Poṣadha</s> in this area of ground — as much as has been claimed by the <s>bhikṣu</s>-<s>Saṅgha</s>, within a circle of the full extent of a man's reach — and should recite the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> <s>Sūtra</s>. This is an informational motion.

body.text: kariṣyati bhante saṃgho imasmin pṛthivīpradeśe yāvatakaṃ bhikṣusaṃghenābhigṛhītaṃ samantanavyāmamātram atrāntare pāñcadaśikaṃ poṣadhaṃ prātimokṣaṃ ca sūtram uddiśiṣyati / kṣamate taṃ saṃghasya, yasmāt tūṣṇīm evam etaṃ dhārayāmi /
body.translated_text: The venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> will perform the fifteenth-day <s>Poṣadha</s> in this area of ground — as much as has been claimed by the <s>bhikṣu</s>-<s>Saṅgha</s>, within a circle of the full extent of a man's reach — and will recite the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> <s>Sūtra</s>. The <s>Saṅgha</s> approves; therefore it is silent — thus I hold it.

body.text: abhimukhaṃ krāmati jarāmaraṇaṃ kṣīyati jīvitendriyaṃ, hāyati saddharmo astameti dharmolko, nirvāyanti deśayitāraḥ, parīttā bhavanti pratipattāraḥ / gacchanti kṣaṇalavamuhūrttarātrindivasamāsārdhamāsaṛtusaṃvatsarāḥ / girinadījalacapalacañcalopamā āyuḥ saṃskārā muhūrttam api nāvatiṣṭhante / apramādenāyuṣmantehi sampādayitavyaṃ / tat kasya hetoḥ? apramādādhigatānāṃ hi tathāgatānām arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ bodhiḥ / apramādādhigato cānuttaro upadhisaṃkṣayo ti vadāmi / tenāpramādenāyuṣmantehi saṃpādayitavyaṃ / daśārthavaśān sampaśyamānās tathāgatārhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ śrāvakāṇām adhiśīlaṃ śikṣāpadaṃ prajñāpayanti, pratimokṣaṃ ca sūtram uddiśanti / katamān daśa? saṃyyathīdaṃ (1) saṃghasaṃgrahāya (2) saṃghasuṣṭhutāya (3) durmaṅkūnāṃ pudgalānāṃ nigrahāya (4) peśalānāṃ ca bhikṣūṇāṃ phāsuvihārāya (5) aprasannānāṃ prasādāya (6) prasannānāṃ ca bhūyobhāvāya dṛṣṭadhārmikāṇām āśravāṇāṃ nirghātāya (8) samparāyikāṇām āśravāṇām āyatyām ananuśravaṇatāya (9) yathemaṃ syāt prāvacanaṃ cirasthitikaṃ (10) bāhujanyaṃ vivṛtaṃ suprakāśitaṃ yāvad devamanuṣyeṣv iti / imān daśārthavaśān saṃpaśyamānās tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhāḥ śrāvakāṇām adhiśīlaṃ śikṣāpadaṃ prajñāpayanti prātimokṣaṃ ca sūtram uddiśanti /
body.translated_text: Old age and death advance; the life-faculty is waning; the true <s>Dharma</s> declines; the lamp of <s>Dharma</s> is setting; the teachers are passing away; the practitioners become few. Moments, instants, hours, nights, days, fortnights, half-months, seasons, and years pass by. Life and conditioned things, like the swift and restless water of a mountain river, do not stand still even for a moment. Venerable ones, you must strive with diligence! For what reason? For the awakening of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the Perfectly Awakened Ones was attained through diligence. And I declare that the unsurpassed destruction of the substrates of existence was attained through diligence. Therefore, venerable ones, you must strive with that diligence. Seeing ten purposes, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones establish training rules of higher moral conduct for their disciples and recite the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> <s>Sūtra</s>. What are those ten? Namely: (1) for the well-being of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, (2) for the comfort of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, (3) for the restraint of ill-behaved individuals, (4) for the comfortable dwelling of well-behaved <s>bhikṣus</s>, (5) for generating faith in those without faith, (6) for the increase of those who have faith, (7) for the destruction of defilements in this present life, (8) for the non-arising of defilements in future lives, (9) so that this dispensation may be long-lasting, (10) widely known, open, and well-illuminated, even among gods and men. Seeing these ten purposes, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones establish training rules of higher moral conduct for their disciples and recite the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> <s>Sūtra</s>.

body.text: prātimokṣam āyuṣmanto sūtram uddiśiṣyāmi / taṃ śṛṇuta sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuruta / bhāṣiṣyāmi / yasya vo siyāpattiḥ so 'viṣkarotu, asantīye āpattīye tūṣṇīṃ bhavitavyaṃ / tūṣṇīmbhāvena kho punar āyuṣmanto pariśuddhā iti vedayiṣyāmi / yathā kho punar āyuṣmanto pratyekaṃ pratyekaṃ pṛcchitasya bhikṣusya vyākaraṇaṃ bhavati evam eva rūpāye bhikṣuparṣāye yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanuśrāvayiṣyati / yo puna bhikṣu evaṃrūpāye bhikṣuparṣāye yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanuśrāviyamāṇo smaramāṇo santīm āpattiṃ nāviṣkaroti saṃprajānamṛṣāvādo se bhavati / saṃprajānamṛṣāvādo kho punar āyuṣmanto āntarāyiko dharmo ukto bhagavatā / tasmāt smaramāṇena bhikṣuṇā āpannena viśuddhiprekṣeṇa santī āpattī āviṣkartavyā / āviṣkṛtvā ca se phāsu bhavati, no anāviṣkṛtvā /
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, I shall recite the <s>Prātimokṣa Sūtra</s>. Listen to it well, thoroughly, and attend to it with your minds. I shall speak. Whoever among you has an offense, let him reveal it. In the absence of an offense, one should remain silent. By the silence, venerable ones, I shall know that you are pure. Just as, when asked individually, a <s>bhikṣu</s> must give his answer, even so in such an assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>, I shall make the announcement up to the third time. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s>, in such an assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>, when the announcement is being made up to the third time, remembering an offense that exists, does not reveal it — for him there is deliberate falsehood. Deliberate falsehood, venerable ones, has been declared by the Blessed One to be an obstructive thing (<s>āntarāyika dharma</s>). Therefore, a <s>bhikṣu</s> who remembers, who has committed [an offense], who desires purification, should reveal an existing offense. Having revealed it, there is well-being for him; not having revealed it, there is not.

body.text: // [iti] nidānaṃ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the Introduction (<s>Nidāna</s>).

body.text: [I. catvāraḥ pārājikā dharmāḥ]
body.translated_text: [I. The Four <s>Pārājika</s> Offenses (Offenses Entailing Defeat)]

body.text: ime kho punar āyuṣmanto catvāraḥ pārājikā dharmā anvardhamāsaṃ sūtre prātimokṣe uddeśam āgacchanti /
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, these four <s>pārājika</s> offenses come up for recitation in the <s>Prātimokṣa Sūtra</s> every half-month.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)Pār.1. yo puna bhikṣu bhikṣūṇāṃ śikṣāsāmīcīsamāpanno śikṣām apratyākhyāya daurbalyam anāviṣkṛtvā maithunaṃ grāmyadharmaṃ pratiṣeveya antamaśato tiryagyonigatāyam api sādham ayaṃ bhikṣuḥ pārājiko bhavaty asaṃvāsyo, na labhate bhikṣūhi sārdhasaṃvāsaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>PrMoSū</s>(Mā-L)<s>Pār</s>.1. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s>, having undertaken the training and communal life of <s>bhikṣus</s>, without having renounced the training, without having declared his weakness, should engage in sexual intercourse, the vulgar practice — even with a female animal — this <s>bhikṣu</s> is defeated (<s>pārājika</s>), no longer in communion. He does not obtain communal living with the <s>bhikṣus</s>.

body.text: idaṃ bhagavatā veśālīyaṃ śikṣāpadaṃ prajñaptaṃ pañcavarṣābhisaṃbuddhena hemantapakṣe pañcame, divase dvādaśame, purebhaktam uttarāmukhaniṣaṇṇena dvyardhapauruṣāyāṃ cchāyāyāṃ, āyuṣmantaṃ yaśikaṃ kalandakaputram ārabhya / imasya ca śikṣāpadasya prajñaptir dharmo, yathāpraṇihitasya ca yā anuvartanatā ayam ucyate anudharmo /
body.translated_text: This training rule was established by the Blessed One at <s>Vaiśālī</s>, in the fifth year after his Awakening, in the fifth [fortnight] of the winter half, on the twelfth day, before the meal, seated facing north, when the shadow was two-and-a-half man-lengths — on account of the venerable <s>Yaśika</s>, son of <s>Kalandaka</s>. The establishment of this training rule is the <s>Dharma</s>; and the compliance with what has been prescribed — that is called the <s>Anudharma</s> (subsidiary rule).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)Pār.2. yo puna bhikṣu grāmād vā araṇyād vā adinnam anyātakaṃ stainasaṃskāram ādiyeya yathārūpeṇādinnādānena [rā]jāno gṛhītvā haneṃsu vā bandheṃsu vā pravrājeṃsu vā hambho puruṣa coro 'si bālo 'si mūḍho 'si stainyo 'sīti vā vadeṃsu, tathārūpaṃ bhikṣur adinnam ādiyamāno ayam pi bhikṣuḥ pārājiko bhavaty asaṃvāsyo, na labhate bhikṣūhi sārdhasaṃvāsaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>PrMoSū</s>(Mā-L)<s>Pār</s>.2. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s> should take, from a village or from the wilderness, what is not given, what belongs to another, with the intention of stealing — in such a way that, for such a taking of what is not given, kings would seize [him] and execute, imprison, or banish [him], or would say: 'Hey, fellow! You are a thief! You are a fool! You are deluded! You are a robber!' — a <s>bhikṣu</s> taking what is not given in such a manner, this <s>bhikṣu</s> too is defeated (<s>pārājika</s>), no longer in communion. He does not obtain communal living with the <s>bhikṣus</s>.

body.text: idaṃ bhagavatā rājagṛhe śikṣāpadaṃ prajñaptaṃ ṣaḍvarṣābhisambuddhena hemantapakṣe dvitī[ye, di]vase navame, paścādbhaktaṃ purastān mukhaniṣaṇṇena aḍḍhātīyapauruṣāyāṃ cchāyāyām āyuṣmantaṃ dhanikaṃ kumbhakārajātīyam ārabhya rājānaṃ ca śreṇīyaṃ bimbasāraṃ pāṃsukūlikaṃ ca bhikṣaṃ / imasya ca śikṣāpadasya prajñaptir dharmo yathāpraṇihitasya ca yā anuvartanatā ayam ucyate anudharmo /
body.translated_text: This training rule was established by the Blessed One at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the sixth year after his Awakening, in the second [fortnight] of the winter half, on the ninth day, after the meal, seated facing east, when the shadow was two-and-a-half man-lengths — on account of the venerable <s>Dhanika</s> of the potter caste, and King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s>, and a rag-robe-wearing <s>bhikṣu</s>. The establishment of this training rule is the <s>Dharma</s>; and the compliance with what has been prescribed — that is called the <s>Anudharma</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)Pār.3. yo puna bhikṣuḥ svahastaṃ manuṣyavigrahaṃ jīvitād vyaparopeya śastrahārakaṃ vāsya paryeṣeya, maraṇāya cainaṃ samādāpeya, maraṇavarṇaṃ vāsya saṃvarṇeya Ō hambho puruṣa kiṃ te iminā pāpakena durjīvitena dhigjīvitena, mṛtaṃ te jīvitāc chreyo Ō iti cittam alaṃ cittasaṃkalpam anekaparyāyeṇa maraṇāya vainaṃ samādāpeya maraṇavarṇaṃ vāsya saṃvarṇeya, so ca puruṣo tenopakrameṇa kālaṃ kuryān nānyena, ayaṃ pi bhikṣuḥ pārājiko bhavaty asaṃvāsyo, na labhate bhikṣūhi sārdhasaṃvāsaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>PrMoSū</s>(Mā-L)<s>Pār</s>.3. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s> should intentionally deprive a human being of life with his own hand, or should seek a weapon-bearer for him, or should incite him to death, or should praise death to him [saying]: 'Hey, fellow! What use is this wretched, evil life to you? Fie upon [such] a life! Death is better for you than life!' — thus, with such a mind, such mental resolve, should in many ways incite him to death or praise death to him, and that person by that means should die, not by another [means] — this <s>bhikṣu</s> too is defeated (<s>pārājika</s>), no longer in communion. He does not obtain communal living with the <s>bhikṣus</s>.

body.text: idaṃ bhagavatā veśālīyaṃ śikṣāpadaṃ prajñaptaṃ ṣaḍvarṣābhisambuddhena hemantapakṣe tṛtīye, divase daśame, paścādbhaktaṃ purastān mukhaniṣaṇṇena aḍḍhātīyapauruṣāyāṃ cchāyāyāṃ sambahulān gilānopasthāpakān bhikṣūn ārabhya mṛgadaṇḍikaṃ ca parivrājakaṃ / imasya ca śikṣāpadasya prajñaptir dharmo, yathāpraṇihitasya ca yā anuvartanatā ayam ucyate anudharmo /
body.translated_text: This training rule was established by the Blessed One at <s>Vaiśālī</s>, in the sixth year after his Awakening, in the third [fortnight] of the winter half, on the tenth day, after the meal, seated facing east, when the shadow was two-and-a-half man-lengths — on account of a number of <s>bhikṣus</s> who attended the sick, and the wanderer <s>Mṛgadaṇḍika</s>. The establishment of this training rule is the <s>Dharma</s>; and the compliance with what has been prescribed — that is called the <s>Anudharma</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)Pār.4. yo puna bhikṣur anabhijānann aparijānann ātmopanāyikam uttarimanuṣyadharmam alamāryajñānadarśanaṃ viśeṣādhigamaṃ prātajāneya ita jānāmi ita paśyāmīti / so tad apareṇa samayena samanugrāhiyamāṇo vā asa[ma]nugrāhiyamāṇo vā āpanno viśuddhiprekṣo evam avaci Ō ajānann evāham āyuṣmanto avaci jānāmi, apaśyan paśyāmīti / iti tucchaṃ mṛṣā vilāpam anyatrābhimānāt* ayaṃ pi bhikṣuḥ pārājiko bhavaty asaṃvāsyo na labhate bhikṣūhi sārdhasaṃvāsaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>PrMoSū</s>(Mā-L)<s>Pār</s>.4. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s>, not knowing, not comprehending, should claim a superhuman state (<s>uttarimanuṣyadharma</s>) pertaining to himself — a noble knowledge and vision, a special attainment — [saying]: 'Thus I know, thus I see.' And if he, at a later time, being examined or not being examined, having committed [the offense], desiring purification, should say thus: 'Not knowing, venerable ones, I said "I know"; not seeing, [I said] "I see" — thus [it was] empty, false talk,' except in the case of overestimation (<s>abhimāna</s>) — this <s>bhikṣu</s> too is defeated (<s>pārājika</s>), no longer in communion. He does not obtain communal living with the <s>bhikṣus</s>.

body.text: idaṃ bhagavatā śrāvastīyaṃ śikṣāpadaṃ prajñaptaṃ ṣaḍvarṣābhisambuddhena hemantapakṣe caturthe, divase trayodaśame, purebhaktaṃ uttarāmukhaniṣaṇṇena aḍḍhucchapauruṣāyāṃ cchāyāyāṃ saṃbahulān grāmavāsikān bhikṣūn ārabhya ābhiyānikaṃ ca bhikṣuṃ / imasya ca śikṣāpadasya prajñaptir dharmo, yathā praṇihitasya ca yā anuvartanatā ayam ucyate anudharmo /
body.translated_text: This training rule was established by the Blessed One at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the sixth year after his Awakening, in the fourth [fortnight] of the winter half, on the thirteenth day, before the meal, seated facing north, when the shadow was half a man's height — on account of a number of <s>bhikṣus</s> dwelling in a village, and a certain <s>bhikṣu</s> who was a follower of the approach [of false claims]. The establishment of this training rule is the <s>Dharma</s>; and the compliance with what has been prescribed — that is called the <s>Anudharma</s>.

body.text:
uddānaṃ
(1) maithunam (2) adinnādānaṃ (3) vadho manuṣyavigrahasyā- (4) bhūtena cottarimanuṣyadharmaṃ pratijānātīti /
body.translated_text:
Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):
(1) Sexual intercourse, (2) taking what is not given, (3) killing of a human being, and (4) falsely claiming a superhuman state — [these are the four].

body.text: uddiṣṭāḥ kho punar āyuṣmanto catvāraḥ pārājikā dharmāḥ / yeṣāṃ bhikṣur ito 'nyatarām āpattim āpadyitvā pārājiko bhavaty asaṃvāsyo na labhate bhikṣūhi sārdhasaṃvāsaṃ / yathā pūrve tathā paścād yathā paścāt tathā pūrve pārājiko bhavaty asaṃvāsyo na labhate bhikṣūhi saṃvāsaṃ ḥ tatrāyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ? dvitīyaṃ pi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ? tṛtīyaṃ pi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ? pariśuddhātrāyuṣmanto yasmāt tūṣṇīm evam etaṃ dhārayāmi ḥ
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, the four <s>pārājika</s> offenses have been recited. A <s>bhikṣu</s> who commits any one of these offenses is defeated (<s>pārājika</s>), no longer in communion — he does not obtain communal living with the <s>bhikṣus</s>. As before, so after; as after, so before — he is defeated, no longer in communion, he does not obtain communal living with the <s>bhikṣus</s>. Herein, venerable ones, I ask: Are you pure? A second time, venerable ones, I ask: Are you pure? A third time, venerable ones, I ask: Are you pure? The venerable ones are pure in this matter, since they remain silent. Thus do I hold it.

body.text: [II. trayodaśa saṃghātiśeṣā dharmāḥ]
body.translated_text: [II. The Thirteen <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s> Offenses (Offenses Requiring Formal Meeting of the <s>Saṃgha</s>)]

body.text: ime kho punar āyuṣmanto trayodaśa saṃghātiśeṣā dharmā anvardhamāsaṃ sūtre prātimokṣe uddeśam āgacchanti /
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, these thirteen <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s> offenses come up for recitation in the <s>Prātimokṣa Sūtra</s> every half-month.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)SA.1. saṃcetanikāye śukrasya visṛṣṭīye anyatra svapnāntare saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>PrMoSū</s>(Mā-L)<s>SA</s>.1. Intentional emission of semen, except during a dream — <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)SA.2. yo puna bhikṣu otīrṇo vipariṇatena cittena mātṛgrāmeṇa sārdhaṃ kāyasaṃsargaṃ samāpadyeya saṃyathīdaṃ hastagrahaṇaṃ vā veṇīgrahaṇaṃ vā anyatarānyatarasya vā punar aṅgajātasya āmoṣaṇaparāmoṣaṇaṃ sādiyeya saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>PrMoSū</s>(Mā-L)<s>SA</s>.2. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s>, overcome [by lust], with a perverted mind, should engage in bodily contact with a woman — namely, grasping the hand, grasping the braid, or touching and caressing any part of the body — and should consent to it — <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)SA.3. yo puna bhikṣu otīrṇo vipariṇatena cittena mātṛgrāmaṃ duṣṭhullāya vācāya obhāṣeya pāpikāya maithunopasaṃhitāya saṃyathīdaṃ yuvāṃ yuvatīti saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>PrMoSū</s>(Mā-L)<s>SA</s>.3. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s>, overcome [by lust], with a perverted mind, should address a woman with lewd speech, wicked [words] connected with sexual intercourse — namely, [calling her] 'young man' or 'young woman' — <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)SA.4. yo puna bhikṣu otīrṇo vipariṇatena cittena mātṛgrāmasya antike ātmikāye paricaryāye varṇaṃ bhāṣeya Ō etad agraṃ bhagini paricaryāṇāṃ yā mādṛśaṃ śramaṇaṃ śīlavantaṃ kalyāṇadharmaṃ brahmacāriṃ etena dharmeṇa upasthiheya paricareya yaduta maithunopasaṃhiteneti saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>PrMoSū</s>(Mā-L)<s>SA</s>.4. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s>, overcome [by lust], with a perverted mind, should praise in the presence of a woman the service of one's own [sexual] need [saying]: 'This, sister, is the highest of services — that you should attend upon and serve one such as me, a virtuous ascetic of good conduct, a celibate, with this practice' — namely, [that] connected with sexual intercourse — <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)SA.5. yo puna bhikṣuḥ saṃcaritraṃ samāpadyeya istriyāye mataṃ puruṣasyopasaṃhareya puruṣasya vā mataṃ istriyāye upasaṃhareya jāyattanena vā jārtanena vā antamaśato tatkṣaṇikāyām api saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>PrMoSū</s>(Mā-L)<s>SA</s>.5. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s> should engage in go-between activity — conveying a woman's [favorable] opinion to a man, or conveying a man's [favorable] opinion to a woman, whether for the purpose of marriage or for the purpose of a concubine, or even for a momentary [liaison] — <s>saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)SA.6. svayaṃ yācikāya bhikṣuṇā kuṭī kārayamāṇena asvāmikātmoddeśikā kuṭī kārāpayitavyā / tatredaṃ pramāṇaṃ Ō dīrghaśo dvādaśa vitastīyo sugatavitastinā / tiryak saptāntaraṃ / bhikṣū cānenābhinetavyā vastudeśanāya / tehi bhikṣuhi vastu deśayitavyaṃ / anāraṃbhaṃ saparikramaṇaṃ / sāraṃbhe ced bhikṣu vastusminn aparikramaṇe svayaṃyācikāya kuṭīṃ kārāpeya asvāmikām ātmoddeśikāṃ bhikṣūn vā nābhineya vastudesanāya, pramāṇaṃ vā atikrameya, adeśite vastusminn aparikramaṇe saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s> 6. When a <s>bhikṣu</s> is having a hut built by begging [for materials] himself, the hut should be made without an owner, for his own use. The measure here is: twelve spans in length by the <s>Sugata</s>'s span, seven [spans] in breadth. And <s>bhikṣus</s> should be brought by him for the inspection of the site. Those <s>bhikṣus</s> should inspect the site — [it should be] free from disturbance and with space to walk around. If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should have a hut built by begging himself, without an owner, for his own use, on a site that involves disturbance and without space to walk around, or should not bring <s>bhikṣus</s> for the inspection of the site, or should exceed the measure, on a site that has not been inspected and without space to walk around — <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)SA.7. mahālakaṃ bhikṣuṇā vihāraṃ [kārā]payamāṇena sasvāmikam ātmoddeśikaṃ bhikṣū cānenābhinetavyā vastudeśanāya / tehi bhikṣūhi vastu deśayitavyaṃ / anāraṃbhaṃ saparikramaṇaṃ / sāraṃbhe ced bhikṣu vastusminn aparikramaṇe mahallakaṃ vihāraṃ kārāpeya sasvāmikam ātmoddeśikaṃ bhikṣūn vā nābhineya vastudeśanāya, adeśite vastusminn aparikramaṇe saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s> 7. When a <s>bhikṣu</s> is having a large monastery (<s>vihāra</s>) built, with an owner, for his own use, <s>bhikṣus</s> should be brought by him for the inspection of the site. Those <s>bhikṣus</s> should inspect the site — [it should be] free from disturbance and with space to walk around. If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should have a large monastery built, with an owner, for his own use, on a site that involves disturbance and without space to walk around, or should not bring <s>bhikṣus</s> for the inspection of the site, on a site that has not been inspected and without space to walk around — <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)SA.8. yo puna bhikṣu bhikṣusya duṣṭo, doṣāt kupito, anāttamano śuddhaṃ bhikṣum anāpattikam amūlakena pārājikena dharmeṇa anudhvaṃseya apy evaṃ nāma imaṃ bhikṣuṃ brahmacaryāto cyāveyaṃ ti, so tad apareṇa samayena samanugrāhiyamāṇo vā asamanugrāhiyamāṇo vā amūlakam eva tam adhikaraṇaṃ bhavati / amūlakasya ca adhikaraṇasya ca adharmo upādinno bhavati, bhikṣu ca doṣe pratiṣṭhihati doṣād avacāmīti saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s> 8. If a <s>bhikṣu</s>, being hostile, angry out of malice, and displeased with a <s>bhikṣu</s>, should accuse a pure <s>bhikṣu</s> who has committed no offense with a groundless <s>Pārājika</s> offense, [thinking:] 'Perhaps in this way I shall cause this <s>bhikṣu</s> to fall from the holy life' — and if, at a later time, whether he is questioned or not questioned, that charge proves to be groundless, and a wrong course of action has been taken in the groundless charge, and the <s>bhikṣu</s> persists in his malice, [saying:] 'I speak out of malice' — <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)SA.9. yo puna bhikṣu bhikṣusya duṣṭo, doṣāt kupito, anāttamano anyabhāgīyasyādhikaraṇasya kiñcid eva leśamātrakaṃ dharmam upādāya aparājikaṃ bhikṣuṃ pārājikena dharmeṇa anudhvaṃseya apy eva nāma imaṃ bhikṣuṃ brahmacaryāto cyāveyaṃ ti, so tad apareṇa samayena samanugrāhiyamāṇo vā asamanugrāhiyamāṇo vā anyabhāgīyam eva tam adhikaraṇaṃ bhavati, anyabhāgīyasya cādhikaraṇasya kocid e[va] leśamātrako dharmo upādinno bhavati, bhikṣu ca doṣe pratiṣṭhihati doṣād avacāmīti saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s> 9. If a <s>bhikṣu</s>, being hostile, angry out of malice, and displeased with a <s>bhikṣu</s>, should seize upon some mere scrap of evidence from a matter belonging to a different category and accuse a non-<s>Pārājika</s> <s>bhikṣu</s> with a <s>Pārājika</s> offense, [thinking:] 'Perhaps in this way I shall cause this <s>bhikṣu</s> to fall from the holy life' — and if, at a later time, whether he is questioned or not questioned, that charge proves to belong to a different category, and some mere scrap of evidence has been taken from a matter belonging to a different category, and the <s>bhikṣu</s> persists in his malice, [saying:] 'I speak out of malice' — <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)SA.10. yo puna bhikṣuḥ samagrasya saṃghasya bhedāya parākrameya bhedanasaṃvartanīyaṃ vādhikaraṇaṃ samādāya pragṛhya tiṣṭheya, so bhikṣu bhikṣūhi evam asya vacanīyo Ō mā āyuṣman samagrasya saṃghasya bhedāya parākramehi, bhedanasaṃvartanīyaṃ vā adhikaraṇaṃ samādāya pragṛhya tiṣṭhāhi / sametu āyuṣmān sārdhaṃ saṃghena, samagro hi saṃgho sahito sammodamāno avivadamāno ekuddeśo kṣīrodakībhūto śāstuḥ śāsanaṃ dīpayamāno sukhaṃ ca phāsuṃ ca viharati / evaṃ ca so bhikṣu bhikṣūhi vucyamāno taṃ vastuṃ pratinissareya ity etaṃ kuśalaṃ / no ca pratinissareya, so bhikṣu bhikṣūhi yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanugrāhitavyo samanubhāṣitavyo tasya vastusya pratinissargāya / yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanugrāhiyamāṇo vā samanubhāṣiyamāṇo vā taṃ vastuṃ pratinissareya ity etaṃ kuśalaṃ / no ca pratinissareya tam eva vastuṃ samādāya pragṛhya tiṣṭheya saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s> 10. If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should strive for the schism of a united <s>Saṃgha</s>, or should take up a dispute conducive to schism and persist in it, that <s>bhikṣu</s> should be addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s> thus: 'Let not the venerable one strive for the schism of a united <s>Saṃgha</s>, nor take up a dispute conducive to schism and persist in it. Let the venerable one be united with the <s>Saṃgha</s>, for a <s>Saṃgha</s> that is united, harmonious, rejoicing together, without quarreling, having a single recitation, blended like milk and water, illuminating the Teacher's teaching, dwells in happiness and comfort.' If that <s>bhikṣu</s>, when thus addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s>, should relinquish that matter — this is well. If he does not relinquish it, that <s>bhikṣu</s> should be formally admonished and exhorted by the <s>bhikṣus</s> up to three times for the relinquishment of that matter. If, being admonished and exhorted up to three times, he relinquishes that matter — this is well. If he does not relinquish it, [but] persists in taking up and holding that very matter — <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)SA.11. tasya kho puna bhikṣusya bhikṣū sahāyakā bhonti eko vā, dvau vā trayo vā saṃbahulā vā, vargavādakā anuvartakāḥ samanujñāḥ saṃghabhedāya / te bhikṣū tān bhikṣūn evaṃ vadeṃsu Ō mā āyuṣmanto etaṃ bhikṣuṃ kiñcid vadatha kalyāṇaṃ vā pāpakaṃ vā / dharmavādī caiṣo bhikṣur vina[ya]vādī caiṣo bhikṣu, asmākaṃ caiṣo bhikṣu cchandaṃ ca ruciṃ ca samādāya pragṛhya vyavaharati / yaṃ caitasya bhikṣusya kṣamate ca rocate ca asmākam api taṃ kṣamate ca rocate ca / jānan caiṣo bhikṣu bhāṣate no ajānan / te bhikṣu bhikṣūhi evam asya vacanīyā Ō mā āyuṣmanto evaṃ vadatha, na eṣo bhikṣur dharmavādī, na eṣo bhikṣur vinayavādī, adharmavādī caiṣo bhikṣu, avinayavādī caiṣo bhikṣu, ajānan* caiṣo bhikṣu bhāṣate no jānan* / mā āyuṣmanto saṃghabhedaṃ rocentu, saṃghasāmagrīm evāyuṣmanto rocentu / samentu āyuṣmanto sārdhaṃ saṃghena / samagro hi sahito sammodamāno avivadamāno ekuddeśo kṣīrodakībhūto śāstuḥ śāsanaṃ dīpayamāno sukhaṃ ca phāsuṃ ca viharati / evaṃ ca te bhikṣū bhikṣūhi vucyamānās taṃ vastuṃ pratinissareṃsu ity etaṃ kuśalaṃ, no ca pratinissareṃsu te bhikṣū bhikṣūhi yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanugrāhitavyāḥ samanubhāṣitavyāḥ tasya vastusya pratinissargāya / yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanugrāhiyamāṇā vā samanubhāṣiyamāṇā vā taṃ vastuṃ pratinissareṃsu i[ty e]taṃ kuśalaṃ, no ca pratinissareṃsu tam eva ca vastuṃ samādāya pragṛhya tiṣṭheṃsu saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s> 11. If that <s>bhikṣu</s> has <s>bhikṣu</s>-companions — one, or two, or three, or several — who are partisans, followers, and supporters of the schism of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and those <s>bhikṣus</s> should say to [other] <s>bhikṣus</s> thus: 'Venerable ones, do not say anything to this <s>bhikṣu</s>, whether good or bad. This <s>bhikṣu</s> is a speaker of the <s>Dharma</s>, this <s>bhikṣu</s> is a speaker of the <s>Vinaya</s>, and this <s>bhikṣu</s> acts having taken up and held our wishes and preferences. What pleases and delights this <s>bhikṣu</s> also pleases and delights us. This <s>bhikṣu</s> speaks knowingly, not unknowingly.' Those <s>bhikṣus</s> should be addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s> thus: 'Let not the venerable ones speak thus. This <s>bhikṣu</s> is not a speaker of the <s>Dharma</s>, this <s>bhikṣu</s> is not a speaker of the <s>Vinaya</s>; this <s>bhikṣu</s> is a speaker of non-<s>Dharma</s>, this <s>bhikṣu</s> is a speaker of non-<s>Vinaya</s>; this <s>bhikṣu</s> speaks unknowingly, not knowingly. Let not the venerable ones take delight in the schism of the <s>Saṃgha</s>; let the venerable ones take delight in the harmony of the <s>Saṃgha</s>. Let the venerable ones be united with the <s>Saṃgha</s>, for a [<s>Saṃgha</s> that is] united, harmonious, rejoicing together, without quarreling, having a single recitation, blended like milk and water, illuminating the Teacher's teaching, dwells in happiness and comfort.' If those <s>bhikṣus</s>, when thus addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s>, should relinquish that matter — this is well. If they do not relinquish it, those <s>bhikṣus</s> should be formally admonished and exhorted up to three times for the relinquishment of that matter. If, being admonished and exhorted up to three times, they relinquish that matter — this is well. If they do not relinquish it, [but] persist in taking up and holding that very matter — <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)SA.12. bhikṣuḥ kho puna durvacakajātīyo bhoti / so uddeśaparyāpannehi śikṣāpadehi bhikṣūhi śikṣāyāṃ saha dharmeṇa saha vinayena vucyamāno ātmānam avacanīyaṃ karoti / so evam āha Ō mā me āyuṣmanto kiñcid vadatha kalyāṇaṃ vā pāpakaṃ vā / aham apy āyuṣmantānāṃ na kiñcid vakṣyāmi kalyāṇaṃ vā pāpakaṃ vā / viramathāyuṣmanto mama vacanāya / so bhikṣu bhikṣūhi evam asya vacanīyo Ō mā āyuṣmann uddeśaparyāpannehi śikṣāpadehi bhikṣūhi śikṣāyāṃ saha dharmeṇa saha vinayena vucyamāno ātmānam avacanīyaṃ karohi / [a]vacanīyam evāyuṣmān ātmānaṃ karotu / bhikṣū pi āyuṣmantaṃ vakṣyanti śikṣāyāṃ saha dharmeṇa saha vina[yena] / āyuṣmān api bhikṣūn vadatu śikṣāyāṃ saha dharmeṇa saha vinayena / evaṃ saṃbaddhā kho punas tasya bhagavato tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksambuddhasya parṣā yad idam anyamanyasya vacanīyā, anyonyāpatti vyutthāpanīyā / evaṃ ca so bhikṣū bhikṣūhi vucyamāno taṃ vastuṃ pratinissareya ity etaṃ kuśalaṃ, no ca pratinissareya so bhikṣu bhikṣūhi yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanugrāhitavyo samanubhāṣitavyo tasya vastusya pratinissargāya / yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanugrāhiyamāṇo vā taṃ vastuṃ pratinissareya ity etaṃ kuśalaṃ, no ca pratinissareya tam eva vastuṃ samādāya pragṛhya tiṣṭheya saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s> 12. A <s>bhikṣu</s> may be of a difficult nature. When that [<s>bhikṣu</s>] is admonished by <s>bhikṣus</s> regarding the training rules included in the recitation, in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> and in accordance with the <s>Vinaya</s>, he renders himself impervious to correction. He says thus: 'Let not the venerable ones say anything to me, whether good or bad. I too shall not say anything to the venerable ones, whether good or bad. Venerable ones, refrain from correcting me.' That <s>bhikṣu</s> should be addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s> thus: 'Let not the venerable one, when admonished by <s>bhikṣus</s> regarding the training rules included in the recitation, in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> and in accordance with the <s>Vinaya</s>, render himself impervious to correction. Rather, let the venerable one render himself open to correction. The <s>bhikṣus</s> too will admonish the venerable one regarding the training, in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> and in accordance with the <s>Vinaya</s>. And let the venerable one admonish the <s>bhikṣus</s> regarding the training, in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> and in accordance with the <s>Vinaya</s>. For thus is the assembly of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, well constituted — namely, [in that members are] willing to be corrected by one another, willing to rehabilitate one another from offenses.' If that <s>bhikṣu</s>, when thus addressed by the <s>bhikṣus</s>, should relinquish that matter — this is well. If he does not relinquish it, that <s>bhikṣu</s> should be formally admonished and exhorted by the <s>bhikṣus</s> up to three times for the relinquishment of that matter. If, being admonished up to three times, he relinquishes that matter — this is well. If he does not relinquish it, [but] persists in taking up and holding that very matter — <s>Saṃghātiśeṣa</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)SA. saṃbahulā bhikṣū kho punar anyataraṃ grāmam vā nagaraṃ vā nigamaṃ vā upaniśrāya viharanti kuladūṣakāḥ pāpasamācārāḥ / teṣāṃ te pāpakāḥ samācārā dṛśyante ca śrūyante ca / kulāny api duṣṭāni dṛśyante ca śrūyante ca / kuladūṣakāś ca punar bhavanti pāpasamācārāḥ / te bhikṣū bhikṣūhi evam asya vacanīyāḥ Ō āyuṣmantānāṃ khalu pāpakāḥ samācārāḥ dṛśyante ca śrūyante ca / kulāny api duṣṭāni dṛśyante ca śrūyante ca / kuladūṣakāś ca punar āyuṣmantaḥ pāpasamācārāḥ / prakramathāyuṣmanto imasmād āvāsād alaṃ vo iha vustena / evaṃ ca te bhikṣū bhikṣūhi vucyamānās te bhikṣū tān bhikṣūn evaṃ vadeṃsu Ō cchandagāmī cāyuṣmanto doṣagāmī cāyuṣmanto saṃgho, mohagāmī cāyuṣmanto saṃgho, bhayagāmī cāyuṣmanto saṃgho, saṃgho ca tāhi tādṛśikāhi āpattīhi ekatyān bhikṣūn pravrājeti ekatyān bhikṣūn na pravrājeti / te bhikṣū bhikṣūhi evam asya vacanīyāḥ Ō mā āyuṣmanto evaṃ vadatha / na saṃgho cchandagāmī, na saṃgho doṣagāmī, na saṃgho mohagāmī, na saṃgho bhayagāmī / na ca saṃgho tāhi tādṛśikāhi āpattīhi ekatyān bhikṣūn pravrājeti, ekatyān bhikṣūn na pravrājeti / āyuṣmantānām eva khalu pāpakāḥ samācārāḥ dṛśyante ca śrūyante ca / kulāny api duṣṭāni dṛśyante ca śrūyante ca / kuladūṣakāś ca punar āyuṣmantaḥ pāpasamācārāḥ / prakramathāyuṣmanto imasmād āvāsād alaṃ vo iha vustena / evaṃ ca te bhikṣū bhikṣūhi vucyamānā taṃ vastuṃ pratinissareṃsu ity etaṃ kuśalaṃ / no ca pratinissareṃsu te bhikṣū bhikṣūhi yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanugrāhitavyā samanubhāṣitavyās tasya vastusya pratinissargāya / yāvantṛtīyakaṃ samanugrāhiyamāṇā vā samanubhāṣiyamāṇā vā taṃ vastuṃ prati[ni]ssareṃsu ity etaṃ kuśalaṃ / no ca pratinissareṃsu tam eva vastuṃ samādāya pragṛhya tiṣṭheṃsu saṃghātiśeṣo /
body.translated_text: If several <s>bhikṣu</s>s dwell in dependence upon a certain village, town, or market-town, and they are corrupters of families and of evil conduct — their evil practices are seen and heard, and the families they have corrupted are seen and heard, and they are corrupters of families and of evil conduct — those <s>bhikṣu</s>s should be told by the [other] <s>bhikṣu</s>s thus: "The evil practices of the venerable ones are seen and heard; the families corrupted [by you] are seen and heard; the venerable ones are corrupters of families and of evil conduct. Depart, venerable ones, from this dwelling. Enough of your residing here." And when those <s>bhikṣu</s>s are thus spoken to by the [other] <s>bhikṣu</s>s, those <s>bhikṣu</s>s say to those <s>bhikṣu</s>s: "The venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> acts out of desire; the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> acts out of hatred; the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> acts out of delusion; the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> acts out of fear. The <s>Saṅgha</s> expels some <s>bhikṣu</s>s for such offenses but does not expel others." Those <s>bhikṣu</s>s should be told by the [other] <s>bhikṣu</s>s thus: "Do not, venerable ones, speak thus. The <s>Saṅgha</s> does not act out of desire; the <s>Saṅgha</s> does not act out of hatred; the <s>Saṅgha</s> does not act out of delusion; the <s>Saṅgha</s> does not act out of fear. The <s>Saṅgha</s> does not expel some <s>bhikṣu</s>s for such offenses while not expelling others. It is indeed the evil practices of the venerable ones that are seen and heard; the families corrupted [by you] are seen and heard; the venerable ones are corrupters of families and of evil conduct. Depart, venerable ones, from this dwelling. Enough of your residing here." If, when those <s>bhikṣu</s>s are thus spoken to by the [other] <s>bhikṣu</s>s, they relinquish that matter — this is good. If they do not relinquish it, those <s>bhikṣu</s>s should be admonished and addressed up to a third time by the [other] <s>bhikṣu</s>s for the relinquishing of that matter. If, when being admonished and addressed up to a third time, they relinquish that matter — this is good. If they do not relinquish it but hold to and cling to that very matter, it is a <s>saṅghātiśeṣa</s> (formal meeting offense).

body.text: // uddānaṃ //
body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

body.text: (1) saṃcetanikā (2) hastagraho (3) obhāṣo (4) paricaryā atha (5) saṃcaritraṃ (6) kuṭīṃ (7) vihāro (8-9) dve cābhūtena (10) saṃghasya ca bhedāyopakrāmati / (11) tasya cānuvartakāḥ (12) durvacako (13) kuladūṣakāś ca //
body.translated_text: (1) Intentional [emission], (2) touching with the hand, (3) lewd speech, (4) personal service, then (5) acting as go-between, (6) a hut, (7) a monastery, (8–9) two [offenses] with false [accusation], (10) and undertaking to split the <s>Saṅgha</s>, (11) and his followers, (12) the difficult to admonish, and (13) the corrupters of families.

body.text: uddiṣṭā kho punar āyuṣmanto trayodaśa saṃghātiśeṣā dharmāḥ / tatra nava prathamāpattikāś catvāro yāvantṛtīyakā, yeṣāṃ bhikṣur ato 'nyatarām āpattim āpadyitvā yāvatakaṃ jānan* cchādeti tāvatakaṃ tena bhikṣuṇā akāmaparivāsaṃ parivasitavyaṃ / parivustaparivāsena bhikṣuṇā uttariṣaḍāhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghe mānatvaṃ caritavyaṃ / cīrṇamānatvo bhikṣuḥ kṛtānudharmo āhvayanapratibaddho yatra syād viṃśagaṇo bhikṣusaṃgho tatra so bhikṣu āhvayitavyo / ekabhikṣuṇāpi ced ūnoviṃśatigaṇo bhikṣusaṃgho taṃ bhikṣum āhveya, so ca bhikṣu anāhūto te ca bhikṣū garhyāḥ / iyam atra sāmīcī /
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, the thirteen <s>saṅghātiśeṣa</s> offenses have been recited. Therein, nine are of the first-offense type and four are of the up-to-three-times type. When a <s>bhikṣu</s> has fallen into any one of these offenses, for as many [days] as he knowingly conceals it, for that many [days] that <s>bhikṣu</s> must undergo involuntary probation (<s>akāmaparivāsa</s>). After completing the probation, the <s>bhikṣu</s> must observe a further six days of penance (<s>mānatva</s>) in the <s>bhikṣu</s>-<s>Saṅgha</s>. A <s>bhikṣu</s> who has completed the penance, who has fulfilled the supplementary procedure (<s>kṛtānudharma</s>), is subject to rehabilitation (<s>āhvayana</s>) — wherever there is a <s>bhikṣu</s>-<s>Saṅgha</s> of twenty members, there that <s>bhikṣu</s> should be rehabilitated. If a <s>bhikṣu</s>-<s>Saṅgha</s> of even one less than twenty should rehabilitate that <s>bhikṣu</s>, that <s>bhikṣu</s> is not rehabilitated, and those <s>bhikṣu</s>s are blameworthy. This is the proper procedure herein.

body.text: tatrāyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ? dvitīyaṃ pi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ? tṛtīyaṃ pi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ? pariśuddhā atrāyuṣmanto yasmāt tūṣṇīm evam etaṃ dhārayāmi /
body.translated_text: Therein I ask the venerable ones: are you pure in this matter? A second time I ask the venerable ones: are you pure? A third time I ask the venerable ones: are you pure? The venerable ones are pure in this matter; since they are silent, thus I hold it.

body.text: [III. duve aniyatā dharmāḥ /]
body.translated_text: [III. The two undetermined offenses (<s>aniyata dharma</s>s)]

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)Aniy. ime kho punar āyuṣmanto duve aniyatā dharmā anvardhamāsaṃ sūtre prātimokṣe uddeśam āgacchanti Ō
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, these two undetermined offenses come up for recitation every half-month in the <s>Sūtra</s> of the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>:

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)Aniy.1. yo puna bhikṣu mātṛgrāmeṇa sārdhaṃ praticchannāsane alaṃkarmaṇīye eko [ekā]ya raho niṣadyāṃ kalpeya, tam enaṃ śraddheyavacasā upāsikā dṛṣṭvā trayāṇāṃ dharmāṇām anyatarānyatareṇa dharmeṇa vadeya pārājikena vā saṃghātiśeṣeṇa vā pācattikena vā / niṣadyāṃ bhikṣuḥ pratijānamāno trayāṇāṃ dharmāṇām anyatarānyatareṇa dharmeṇa kārāpayitavyo pārājikena vā saṃghātiśeṣeṇa vā pācattikena vā yena yena vā punar asya śraddheyavacasā upāsikā dṛṣṭvā dharmeṇa vadeya, tena so bhikṣu dharmeṇa kārāpayitavyo / ayaṃ dharmo aniyato /
body.translated_text: If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should sit alone with a woman in a concealed seat suitable for the act [of sexual intercourse], one with one in private, and a trustworthy <s>upāsikā</s> (laywoman), having seen [them], should accuse him of any one of three offenses — a <s>pārājika</s> (defeat), a <s>saṅghātiśeṣa</s>, or a <s>pācattika</s> (confession) — the <s>bhikṣu</s> who acknowledges the sitting should be dealt with according to any one of those three offenses: a <s>pārājika</s>, a <s>saṅghātiśeṣa</s>, or a <s>pācattika</s> — or according to whichever offense the trustworthy <s>upāsikā</s>, having seen [them], accuses him of, that <s>bhikṣu</s> should be dealt with according to that offense. This offense is undetermined (<s>aniyata</s>).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)Aniy.2. na haiva kho punaḥ praticchannāsanaṃ bhavati, nālaṃ karmaṇīyaṃ, alaṃ kho puna mātṛgrāmaṃ duṣṭhullāya vācāya obhāṣituṃ pāpikāya maithunopasaṃhitāya / tathārūpe ca bhikṣu āsane mātṛgrāmeṇa sārdham eko ekāya raho niṣadyāṃ kalpeya, tam enaṃ śraddheyavacasā upāsikā dṛṣṭvā dvinnāṃ dharmāṇām anyatarānyatareṇa dharmeṇa vadeya saṃghātiśeṣeṇa vā pācattikena vā / niṣadyāṃ bhikṣuḥ pratijānamāno dvinnāṃ dharmāṇām anyatarāntareṇa dharmeṇa kārāpayitavyo saṃghātiśeṣeṇa vā pācattikena vā, yena yena vā punar asya śraddheyavacasā upāsikā dṛṣṭvā dharmeṇa vadeya, tena tena so bhikṣu dharmeṇa kārāpayitavyo / ayaṃ pi dharmo aniyato /
body.translated_text: But if the seat is not concealed and not suitable for the act [of sexual intercourse], yet suitable for speaking lewd and evil words to a woman, connected with sexual intercourse, and in such a seat a <s>bhikṣu</s> should sit alone with a woman, one with one in private, and a trustworthy <s>upāsikā</s>, having seen [them], should accuse him of any one of two offenses — a <s>saṅghātiśeṣa</s> or a <s>pācattika</s> — the <s>bhikṣu</s> who acknowledges the sitting should be dealt with according to any one of those two offenses: a <s>saṅghātiśeṣa</s> or a <s>pācattika</s> — or according to whichever offense the trustworthy <s>upāsikā</s>, having seen [them], accuses him of, that <s>bhikṣu</s> should be dealt with according to that offense. This offense too is undetermined.

body.text: // uddānaṃ //
body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

body.text: (1) praticchannāsanaṃ (2) rahoniṣadyā ca /
body.translated_text: (1) A concealed seat and (2) private sitting.

body.text: uddiṣṭāḥ kho punar āyuṣmanto duve aniyatā dharmāḥ / tatrāyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ? dvitīyaṃ pi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhā? tṛtīyaṃ pi āyuṣmanto pṛcchāmi kaccittha pariśuddhāḥ? pariśuddhā atrāyuṣmanto yasmāt tūṣṇīm evam etaṃ dhārayāmi /
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, the two undetermined offenses have been recited. Therein I ask the venerable ones: are you pure in this matter? A second time I ask the venerable ones: are you pure? A third time I ask the venerable ones: are you pure? The venerable ones are pure in this matter; since they are silent, thus I hold it.

body.text: [IV. triṃśan nissargikapācattikā dharmāḥ]
body.translated_text: [IV. The thirty forfeiture-confession (<s>nissargikapācattika</s>) offenses]

body.text: ime kho punar āyuṣmanto triṃśan nissargikapācattikā dharmā anvardhamāsaṃ sūtre prātimokṣe uddeśam āgacchanti Ō
body.translated_text: Venerable ones, these thirty forfeiture-confession offenses come up for recitation every half-month in the <s>Sūtra</s> of the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>:

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.1. kṛtacīvarehi bhikṣūhi uddhṛtasmin kaṭhine daśāhaparamaṃ bhikṣuṇā atirekacīvaraṃ dhārayitavyaṃ / taduttariṃ dhāreya, nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: When the robes of the <s>bhikṣu</s>s have been made and the <s>kaṭhina</s> (robe-frame) has been withdrawn, a <s>bhikṣu</s> may keep an extra robe for at most ten days. If he keeps it beyond that, it is a forfeiture-confession (<s>nissargikapācattika</s>).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.2. kṛtacīvarehi bhikṣūhi uddhṛtasmin kaṭhine ekarātraṃ pi ced bhikṣuḥ trayāṇāṃ cīvarāṇām anyatarānyatareṇa vipravaseya anyatra saṃghasaṃmutīye, nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: When the robes of the <s>bhikṣu</s>s have been made and the <s>kaṭhina</s> has been withdrawn, if a <s>bhikṣu</s> should spend even one night apart from any one of the three robes, except with the consent of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, it is a forfeiture-confession.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.3. kṛtacīvarehi bhikṣūhi uddhṛtasmin kaṭhine utpadyeya bhikṣusya akālacīvaram ākāṃkṣamāṇena bhikṣuṇā pratigṛhṇitavyaṃ / pratigṛhṇitvā kṣipram eva taṃ cīvaraṃ kārāpayitavyaṃ / kārāpayato ca tasya bhikṣusya taṃ cīvaraṃ na paripūreya, māsaparamaṃ tena bhikṣuṇā taṃ cīvaraṃ nikṣipitavyaṃ ūnasya pāripūrīye santīye pratyāśāye / taduttariṃ nikṣipeya santīye vā asantīye vā pratyāśāye nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: When the robes of the <s>bhikṣu</s>s have been made and the <s>kaṭhina</s> has been withdrawn, if an unseasonable robe should arise for a <s>bhikṣu</s>, the <s>bhikṣu</s> who wishes may accept it. Having accepted it, he should have that robe made up quickly. If, while having that robe made, it is not completed for that <s>bhikṣu</s>, that <s>bhikṣu</s> may store that robe for at most one month in expectation of completing what is lacking. If he stores it beyond that, whether or not there is expectation [of completion], it is a forfeiture-confession.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.4. yo puna bhikṣur anyātikāye bhikṣuṇīye cīvaraṃ pratigṛhṇeya anyatra pallaṭṭhakena nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should accept a robe from a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> who is not a relative, except in exchange, it is a forfeiture-confession.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.5. yo puna bhikṣur anyātikāye bhikṣuṇīye purāṇacīvaraṃ dhovāpeya vā rañjāpeya vā ākoṭāpeya vā nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should have a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> who is not a relative wash, dye, or beat a used robe, it is a forfeiture-confession.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.6. yo puna bhikṣur anyātakaṃ gṛhapatiṃ vā gṛhapatiputraṃ [?Śtipatinīṃ] vā cīvaraṃ yāceya anyatra samaye nissargikapācattikaṃ / tatrāyaṃ samayo Ō ācchinnacīvaro bhikṣur bhavati / ayam atra samayo /
body.translated_text: If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should beg a robe from a householder or a householder’s son [or wife] who is not a relative, except at the proper time, it is a forfeiture-confession. This is the proper time: the <s>bhikṣu</s> has had his robe stolen. This is the proper time herein.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.7. ācchinnacīvareṇa bhikṣuṇā kṣamate anyātakaṃ gṛhapatiṃ vā gṛhapatiputrīṃ [Śtipatinīṃ] vā cīvaraṃ yācituṃ / tam enam abhihṛṣṭo samāno saṃbahulehi cīvarehi pravāreya, tathāpravāritena bhikṣuṇā sāntarottaraparamaṃ cīvaraṃ sādayitavyaṃ / taduttariṃ sādiyeya nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: When a <s>bhikṣu</s> whose robe has been stolen is permitted to beg a robe from a householder or a householder’s daughter [or wife] who is not a relative, and if [the householder], being generous, should offer him many robes, that <s>bhikṣu</s>, thus offered, should accept at most an inner and an upper robe. If he accepts beyond that, it is a forfeiture-confession.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.8. bhikṣuṃ kho punar uddiśya anyatareṣāṃ dvinnāṃ gṛhapatikānāṃ cīvaracetāpanāny abhisaṃskṛtāni bhavanti abhisaṃcetayitāni Ō imehi vayaṃ cīvaracetāpanehi civaraṃ cetāpayitvā itthanāmaṃ bhikṣuṃ cīvareṇācchadayiṣyāmaḥ / tatra ca bhikṣuḥ pūrvaṃ apravārito upasaṃkramitvā vikalpam āpadyeya Ō sādhu kho puna yūyam āyuṣmanto imehi cīvaracetāpanehi cīvaraṃ cetāpayitvā itthaṃnāmaṃ bhikṣuṃ cīvareṇācchādetha / evaṃrūpeṇa vā [evaṃrūpeṇa vā] ubhau pi sahitau ekena kalyāṇakāmatām upādāya / abhiniṣpanne cīvare ni[ssa]rgikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: NP.8. If robe-funds have been prepared and set aside by any two householders, designating a <s>bhikṣu</s>, [thinking:] 'With these robe-funds we shall purchase a robe and clothe the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so' — and that <s>bhikṣu</s>, without having been previously invited, approaches and makes a specification [saying:] 'It would be good indeed, venerable sirs, if you were to purchase a robe with these robe-funds and clothe the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so with [a robe] of such-and-such a kind or of such-and-such a kind,' [thus] bringing both together into one out of desire for something fine — when the robe is finished, it is a <s>nissargikapācattika</s> (forfeiture-expiation offense).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.9. bhikṣuṃ kho punar uddiśya anyatareṣāṃ dvinnāṃ gṛhapatikasya gṛhapatinīye ca pratyekacīvaracetāpanāni abhisaṃskṛtāni bhavanti, abhisaṃcetayitāni Ō imehi vayaṃ pratyekacīvaracetāpanehi pratyekaṃ pratyekaṃ cīvaraṃ cetāpayitvā itthaṃnāmaṃ bhikṣuṃ pratyekaṃ pratyekaṃ cīvareṇācchadayiṣyāmaḥ / tatra ca bhikṣuḥ pūrvaṃ apravārito upasaṃkramitvā vikalpam āpadyeya Ō sādhu kho punas tvam āyuṣman, tvaṃ ca bhagini, imehi pratyekacīvaracetāpanehi pratyekaṃ cīvaraṃ cetāpayitvā itthaṃnāmaṃ bhikṣuṃ pratyekaṃ cīvareṇācchādetha evaṃrūpeṇa vā evaṃrūpeṇa vā ubhau pi sahitau ekena kalyāṇakāmatām upādāya / abhiniṣpanne cīvare nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: NP.9. If separate robe-funds have been prepared and set aside by any two — a householder and a householder's wife — designating a <s>bhikṣu</s>, [thinking:] 'With these separate robe-funds we shall each purchase a robe and separately clothe the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so' — and that <s>bhikṣu</s>, without having been previously invited, approaches and makes a specification [saying:] 'It would be good indeed, venerable sir, if you and you, sister, were to purchase a robe with these separate robe-funds and separately clothe the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so with [a robe] of such-and-such a kind or of such-and-such a kind,' [thus] bringing both together into one out of desire for something fine — when the robe is finished, it is a <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.10. bhikṣuṃ kho punar uddiśya anyataro rājā vā rājabhogyo vā dūtena cīvaracetāpanāni preṣeya / so bhikṣus tenopasaṃkramitvā taṃ bhikṣum evaṃ vadeya Ō imāni khalv āryam uddiśya itthaṃnāmena rājñā ca rājabhogyena vā dūtena cīvaracetāpanāni preṣitāni, tāni āryo pratigṛhṇātu / tena bhikṣuṇā so dūto evam asya vacanīyo Ō na kho punar āyuṣman kṣamate bhikṣusya cīvaracetāpanāni pratigṛhṇituṃ / cīvaraṃ tu vayaṃ pratigṛhṇāmaḥ kālena samayena kalpikaṃ dīyamānaṃ / evam ukte so dūto taṃ bhikṣum evaṃ vadeya [sa]nti punar ārya kecid bhikṣūṇāṃ vaiyāpṛtyakarāti / ākāṃkṣamāṇena bhikṣuṇā santā vaiyāpṛtyakarā vyapadiśitavyāḥ ārāmikā vā / ete āyuṣman bhikṣūṇāṃ vaiyāpṛtyakarā ye bhikṣūṇāṃ vaiyāpṛtyaṃ karonti / evam ukte so dūto yena vaiyāpṛtyakarās tenopasaṃkramitvā tān vaiyāpṛtyakarān evaṃ vadeya Ō sādhu kho puna yūyam āyuṣmanto vaiyāpṛtyakarā imehi cīvaracetāpanehi cīvaraṃ cetāpayitvā itthaṃnāma bhikṣuṃ cīvareṇācchādetha kālena samayena kalpikenānavadyena / so ca dūto tān vaiyāpṛtyakarān saṃjñapayitvā yena so bhikṣus tenopasaṃkramitvā na bhikṣum eva vadeya ye khu te āryeṇa vaiyāpṛtyakarā vyapadiṣṭās te mayā saṃjñaptās tān upasaṃkrameyāmi / ācchādayiṣyanti te cīvareṇa kālena samayena kalpikenānavadyena / ākāṃkṣamāṇena bhikṣuṇā cīvarārthikena [yena] te vaiyāpṛtyakarās tenopasaṃkramitvā te vaiyāpṛtyakarāḥ sakṛt* dvikkhutto trikkhutto codayitavyā vijñāpayitavyāḥ Ō artho āyuṣmanto bhikṣusya cīvareṇeti / sakṛt* dvikkhutto trikkhutto codayanto vijñāpayanto taṃ cīvaram abhiniṣpādeya ity etat kuśalaṃ, no ced abhiniṣpādeya catukkhutto pañcakhutto ṣaṭkhuttoparamaṃ tena bhikṣuṇā tūṣṇībhūtena uddeśe sthātavyaṃ / catukkhutto pañcakkhutto ṣaṭkkhuttoparamaṃ tūṣṇībhūto uddeśe tiṣṭhanto taṃ cīvaram abhiniṣpādeya, ity etat kuśalaṃ, no ced abhiniṣpādeya tad uttapanto vā vyāyamanto vā taṃ cīvaram abhiniṣpādeya, abhiniṣpanne cīvare nissargikapācattikaṃ / no ced abhiniṣpādeya yena se tāni rājñā vā rājabhogyena vā dūtena cīvaracetāpanāni preṣitāni tatra tena bhikṣuṇā svayaṃ vā gantavyaṃ, dūto vā pratirūpo preṣayitavyo, yāni khu āyuṣmantehi itthaṃnāmaṃ bhikṣum uddiśya dūtena cīvaracetāpanāni preṣitāni na khu tāni tasya bhikṣusya kiñcid arthaṃ spharanti, pratyanveṣatha, na svakaṃ dharmo / vo vipraṇaśiṣyatīti iyam atra sāmīcī /
body.translated_text: NP.10. If any king or royal official sends robe-funds by a messenger, designating a <s>bhikṣu</s>, that messenger should approach and say to that <s>bhikṣu</s>: 'These robe-funds have been sent by the king or royal official named so-and-so, designating the venerable one; let the venerable one accept them.' That <s>bhikṣu</s> should say to the messenger thus: 'It is not proper, venerable sir, for a <s>bhikṣu</s> to accept robe-funds. But we do accept a robe, at the proper time and season, when it is allowable and given.' When this has been said, if the messenger says to that <s>bhikṣu</s>: 'Are there, venerable sir, any attendants for the <s>bhikṣus</s>?' — the <s>bhikṣu</s> who wishes [to receive a robe] should point out the existing attendants [or] monastery servants: 'These, venerable sir, are the attendants of the <s>bhikṣus</s> who perform services for the <s>bhikṣus</s>.' When this has been said, the messenger should approach those attendants and say to them: 'It would be good indeed, venerable attendants, if you were to purchase a robe with these robe-funds and clothe the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so, at the proper time and season, with [a robe that is] allowable and blameless.' Having instructed those attendants, the messenger should approach that <s>bhikṣu</s> and say: 'The attendants whom the venerable one pointed out — I have instructed them; let the venerable one approach them; they will clothe you with a robe at the proper time and season, with [one that is] allowable and blameless.' The <s>bhikṣu</s> who desires [a robe] and needs a robe should approach those attendants and prompt and inform them once, twice, or three times: 'The <s>bhikṣu</s> needs a robe, venerable sirs.' If, by prompting and informing once, twice, or three times, he obtains the robe, that is good. If he does not obtain it, he should stand silently at the showing [of the attendants] a fourth, fifth, and sixth time at most. If, standing silently at the showing a fourth, fifth, and sixth time at most, he obtains the robe, that is good. If he does not obtain it, and [then] by urging or exerting himself he obtains the robe — when the robe is finished, it is a <s>nissargikapācattika</s>. If he does not obtain it, then the <s>bhikṣu</s> himself should go, or send a suitable messenger, to [the person] by whom those robe-funds were sent through the king or royal official [saying:] 'The robe-funds which the venerable ones sent by messenger designating the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so — those are of no use whatsoever to that <s>bhikṣu</s>. Seek [them] back; let not your own property be lost.' This is the proper procedure in this matter.

body.text: // uddānaṃ //
body.translated_text: // Summary verse //

body.text: (1) daśāhaṃ (2) vipravāso (3) akāle ca (4) pratigraho (5) dhovanā (6) yācanā caṃva / (7) sāntarottaraṃ (8-9) dve ca vikalpena (10) rājā ca // prathamo vargaḥ //
body.translated_text: (1) Ten days, (2) separation, (3) and out of season, (4) acceptance, (5) washing, (6) and also begging, (7) with inner and outer [robe], (8-9) and two [rules] regarding specification, (10) and the king. // First section. //

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.11. yo puna bhikṣuḥ śuddhakālakānām eḍakalomānāṃ navaṃ santhataṃ kārāpeya nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: NP.11. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s> should have a new felt [rug] made entirely of black sheep's wool — it is a <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.12. navaṃ santhataṃ bhikṣuṇā kārāpayamāṇena śuddhakālakānām eḍakalomānāṃ dve bhāgā ādayitavyās tṛtīyo odātikānāṃ caturtho gocarikāṇāṃ / taduttarim ādiyeya nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: NP.12. When a <s>bhikṣu</s> is having a new felt [rug] made, two parts of black sheep's wool are to be taken, a third of white, and a fourth of brown. If he takes more than that — it is a <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.13. yo puna bhikṣuḥ kauśeyamiśrāṇām eḍakalomānāṃ navaṃ santhataṃ kārāpeya nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: NP.13. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s> should have a new felt [rug] made of sheep's wool mixed with silk — it is a <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.14. navaṃ santhataṃ bhikṣuṇā kārāpayamāṇena akāmaṃ ṣaḍvarṣāṇi dhārayitavyaṃ / tato ca bhikṣuḥ pratyoreṇa taṃ purāṇaṃ santhataṃ visarjayitvā vā avisarjayitvā vā anyaṃ navaṃ santhataṃ kārāpeya kalyāṇakāmatām upādāya, anyatra namatasaṃmutīye nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: NP.14. A new felt [rug] made by a <s>bhikṣu</s> must be kept for at least six years. If that <s>bhikṣu</s>, within less [than six years], whether having discarded the old felt [rug] or not, should have another new felt [rug] made, out of desire for something fine, except with the consent of the <s>Saṅgha</s> — it is a <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.15. navaṃ santhataniṣīdanaṃ bhikṣuṇā kārāpayamāṇena tato purāṇasanthatāto samantāt sugatavitastinā bhāgo ādayitavyo navasya durvaṇṇīkaraṇārthaṃ / tato ca bhikṣur anādāya navasanthataṃ niṣīdanaṃ kārāpeya nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: NP.15. When a <s>bhikṣu</s> is having a new felt sitting-mat made, a piece the size of a <s>Sugata</s>-span on all sides is to be taken from the old felt [rug] for the purpose of disfiguring the new one. If that <s>bhikṣu</s>, without taking [a piece from the old], should have a new felt sitting-mat made — it is a <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.16. bhikṣusya kho punar adhvānamārge pratipannasya utpadyeṃsu e[ḍa]kalomāni / ākāṃkṣamāṇena bhikṣuṇā pratigṛhṇitavyaṃ / pratigṛhṇitvā sāmaṃ triyojanaparamaṃ hartavyam asante anyasmi[n] hārake taduttariṃ hāreya sante vā asante vā anyasmi[n] hārake, nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: NP.16. If sheep's wool should come into the possession of a <s>bhikṣu</s> who is traveling on a road, and the <s>bhikṣu</s> wishes, he may accept it. Having accepted it, he may carry it himself for three <s>yojanas</s> at most, when there is no other person to carry it. If he carries it farther than that, whether there is another person to carry it or not — it is a <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.17. yo puna bhikṣur anyātikāye bhikṣuṇīye eḍakalomādi dhovāpeya vā raṃjāpe[ya] vā vivaṭāpaye vā, nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: NP.17. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s> should have sheep's wool and the like washed, dyed, or carded by a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> who is not a relative — it is a <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.18. yo puna bhikṣuḥ svahastaṃ jātarūparajatam udgṛhṇeya vā udgṛhṇāpeya vā antamasato iha nikṣipehīti vā vadeya, upanikṣiptaṃ vā sādiyeya nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: NP.18. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s> should accept gold or silver with his own hand, or have it accepted [by another], or even say 'deposit it here,' or should consent to it being deposited [for him] — it is a <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.19. yo puna bhikṣur anekavidhaṃ krayavikrayavyavahāraṃ samāpadyeya saṃyyathīdaṃ imaṃ kriṇa ito kriṇa ettakamettake[na krī]ṇāhīti vā vadeya, nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: NP.19. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s> should engage in various kinds of buying-and-selling transactions, namely saying 'Buy this, buy that, buy so much for so much' — it is a <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.20. yo puna bhikṣur anekavidhaṃ jātarūparajatavikṛtivyavahāraṃ samāpadyeya nissargikapācattikam //
body.translated_text: NP.20. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s> should engage in various kinds of exchange transactions involving gold and silver — it is a <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: // uddānaṃ //
body.translated_text: // Summary verse //

body.text: (11) śuddhakālakānāṃ (12) dve bhāgā (13) kauśeyamiśra (14) ṣaḍvarṣāṇi (15) niṣīdanaṃ (16) adhvānamārgo (17) vivaṭā vā (18) svahastaṃ (19) krayavikraya (20) vikṛtivyavahāreṇa // dvitīyo vargaḥ //
body.translated_text: (11) Entirely black, (12) two parts, (13) mixed with silk, (14) six years, (15) sitting-mat, (16) road-journey, (17) or carding, (18) with one's own hand, (19) buying-and-selling, (20) exchange transactions. // Second section. //

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.21. daśāhaparamaṃ bhikṣuṇā atirekapātraṃ dhārayitavyaṃ / taduttariṃ dhāreya nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: NP.21. A <s>bhikṣu</s> may keep an extra bowl for ten days at most. If he keeps it longer — it is a <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.22. yo puna bhikṣu ūnapañcabandhanabaddhena pātreṇa anyaṃ navaṃ pātraṃ paryeṣeya kāmātām upādāya, tena bhikṣuṇā taṃ pātraṃ bhikṣuparṣāye nissaritavyaṃ / yo tahi bhikṣuparṣāye pātraparyanto bhavati so tasya bhikṣusya anupradātavyo Ō evaṃ te āyuṣman pātro dhārayitavyo yāvad bhedanaṃ, nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>PrMoSū</s>(Mā-L)<s>NP</s>.22. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s>, having a bowl with fewer than five mends, should seek another new bowl out of desire — that <s>bhikṣu</s> must forfeit that bowl to the assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>. Whatever is the last bowl in the assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>, that should be given to that <s>bhikṣu</s> [with the words]: 'Thus, venerable one, this bowl should be kept by you until it breaks' — <s>nissargikapācattika</s> (offense requiring forfeiture and expiation).

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.23. yāni kho punar imāni gilānapratiṣevaṇīyāni bhaiṣajyāni bhavanti sayyathīdaṃ sarpistailamadhuphāṇitaṃ Ō evaṃrūpāṇi gilānena bhikṣuṇā satkṛtyābhigṛhītāni, kṣamate saptāhaṃ sannidhikāraṃ paribhuñjituṃ, santaṃ śeṣaṃ nissaritavyaṃ tad uttaritavyaṃ / taduttariṃ khādeya vā bhuṃjeya vā santaṃ vā śeṣabhū[taṃ] nissareya nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>PrMoSū</s>(Mā-L)<s>NP</s>.23. There are medicines to be used by the sick — namely, ghee, oil, honey, and sugar. Such [medicines], properly received by a sick <s>bhikṣu</s>, may be stored and consumed for seven days. Any remainder should be forfeited and disposed of. If [a <s>bhikṣu</s>] should chew or eat beyond that, or should forfeit any remaining [after the period] — <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.24. yo puna bhikṣu bhikṣusya cīvaraṃ datvā yathā duṣṭo doṣāt kupito anāttamāno ācchindeya vā ācchindāpayeya vā Ō āhara bhikṣu cīvaraṃ, na te 'haṃ demīti vā vadeya, nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>PrMoSū</s>(Mā-L)<s>NP</s>.24. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s>, having given a robe to a <s>bhikṣu</s>, should then, angered, furious, wrathful, and displeased, seize it back or cause it to be seized back [saying]: 'Give back the robe, <s>bhikṣu</s>! I do not give it to you!' — <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.25. māso śeṣo grīṣmāṇām iti bhikṣuṇā varṣāsāṭikācīvaraṃ paryeṣitavyaṃ / ardhamāso avaśiṣṭo ti kṛtvā snapitavyam / tato ca bhikṣuḥ pra[tyo]reṇa varṣāsāṭikācīvaraṃ paryeṣeya, kṛtvā vā snāpeya, nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>PrMoSū</s>(Mā-L)<s>NP</s>.25. When one month of summer remains, a <s>bhikṣu</s> should seek a rain-bathing cloth (<s>varṣāsāṭikā cīvara</s>). When half a month remains, it should be put to use. If a <s>bhikṣu</s> should seek a rain-bathing cloth before [that time], or should use it before [that time] — <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.26. yo puna bhikṣuḥ svayaṃyācikāya sūtraṃ tantuvāyena cīvaraṃ vunāpeya nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>PrMoSū</s>(Mā-L)<s>NP</s>.26. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s> should have a robe woven by a weaver with thread obtained by begging on his own — <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.27. bhikṣuṃ kho punar uddiśya anyataro gṛhapatir vā gṛhapatiputro vā tantuvāyena cīvaraṃ vunāpeya, tena ca bhikṣuḥ pūrvaṃ apravārito upasaṃkramitvā vikalpam āpadyeya Ō sādhu kho punas tvam āyuṣmann imaṃ cīvaram āyataṃ ca karohi, vistṛtaṃ ca karohi, suvutaṃ ca karohi, sutacchitaṃ ca karohi, suvilikhitaṃ ca karohi / apy eva nāma vayaṃ pi tava kiñcid eva mātrām upasaṃharema, māṣakaṃ vā māṣakārhaṃ vā piṇḍapātaṃ vā piṇḍapātārhaṃ vā / tatra ca so bhikṣur evaṃ vaditvā na kiñcid eva mātrām upasaṃhareya māṣakaṃ vā māṣakārhaṃ vā piṇḍapātaṃ vā piṇḍapātārhaṃ vā, abhiniṣpanne cīvare nissargikapācattikaṃ /
body.translated_text: <s>PrMoSū</s>(Mā-L)<s>NP</s>.27. If a certain householder or householder's son should have a robe woven by a weaver for a <s>bhikṣu</s>, and that <s>bhikṣu</s>, not previously invited, should approach [the weaver] and express a preference [saying]: 'It would be good, venerable one, if you make this robe long and wide, well-woven, well-leveled, and well-finished. Perhaps we might offer you some small gift in return — a <s>māṣaka</s> coin, or the equivalent of a <s>māṣaka</s>, or alms-food, or the equivalent of alms-food.' And if that <s>bhikṣu</s>, having spoken thus, does not offer even a small gift — a <s>māṣaka</s> or its equivalent, alms-food or its equivalent — when the robe is completed — <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.28. daśāhānāgataṃ kho puna tremāsaṃ kārttikī paurṇamāsī utpadyeya bhikṣusya ātyāyikaṃ cīvaram ātyāyikaṃ manyamāno na bhikṣuṇā pratigṛhṇitavyaṃ / pratigṛhṇitvā yāvac cīvaradānakālasamayaṃ nikṣipitavyaṃ / taduttariṃ nikṣipeya nissargikapācattikam /
body.translated_text: <s>PrMoSū</s>(Mā-L)<s>NP</s>.28. When the three months [before] the full-moon of <s>Kārttikī</s> arise with ten days remaining, if there should appear for a <s>bhikṣu</s> an urgent robe — the <s>bhikṣu</s>, considering it urgent, should accept it. Having accepted it, it should be kept until the time and season for robe-distribution. If [he] should keep it beyond that — <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.29. upavarṣaṃ kho punaḥ tremāsaṃ kārttikī paurṇamāsī bhikṣu cāraṇyake śayanāsane viharanti samaye sapratibhaye sāśaṃkasaṃmate / ākāṃkṣamāṇena bhikṣuṇā trayāṇāṃ cīvarāṇām anyatarānyataraṃ cīvaram antaragṛhe nikṣipitavyaṃ, syāt tasya bhikṣusya kocid eva pratyayo tasmāc cīvarād vipravāsāya, ṣaḍāhaparamaṃ tena bhikṣuṇā tasmāc cīvarād vipravasitavyaṃ / taduttariṃ vipravaseya anyatra bhikṣu saṃmutīye nissargikapācattikam /
body.translated_text: <s>PrMoSū</s>(Mā-L)<s>NP</s>.29. When the three months after the rains [beginning with] the full-moon of <s>Kārttikī</s> [have passed], <s>bhikṣus</s> dwelling in forest lodgings in a season that is feared, suspected, and considered dangerous — if a <s>bhikṣu</s> who desires [to do so] should store any one of the three robes in an inhabited area, and there is some reason for that <s>bhikṣu</s> to be separated from that robe — he may be separated from that robe for six nights at most. If he should be separated [from it] beyond that, except with the permission of the <s>bhikṣus</s> — <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: PrMoSū(Mā-L)NP.30. yo puna bhikṣur jānan sāṃghikāṃ lābhaṃ saṃghe pariṇatam ātmano pariṇāmeya nissargikapācattikam //
body.translated_text: <s>PrMoSū</s>(Mā-L)<s>NP</s>.30. Whatever <s>bhikṣu</s>, knowingly, should divert a gain belonging to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, designated for the <s>Saṃgha</s>, to himself — <s>nissargikapācattika</s>.

body.text: // uddānaṃ //
body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

body.text: (21) pātra (22) bandhanaṃ (23) bhaiṣajyam (24) ācchedo (25) varṣāśāṭikā / (26-27) tantuvāyena dve (28) daśāhānāgatam (29) upavarṣaṃ (30) pariṇāmanena // tṛtīyo vargaḥ //
